utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Since there are no preliminaries, Mr. Plahuta, I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Jordash will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Jordash, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Plahuta.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I just to want to pick up very briefly on the issue of the military department in Bajina Basta where you registered. You testified about the idea of being a contract soldier and registering in the military department in Bajina Basta, and you stated that afterwards the individual would be deployed in units on the border of the Drina within the framework of the Uzice Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The Uzice Corps, at that time, was conducting military operations to protect the border; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When you went to register at the military department, were you told or given an option of where you might be deployed?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were only told that we would all be deployed along the border in the area of the Uzice Corps along the Drina. They didn't specify the watch-tower, but they said that it was to be in the environs of Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So everybody registering at the military department would be deployed within Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the only part of the Uzice Corps which went into Bosnia were the special brigades that we were talking about yesterday, the 68th Guards, the 72nd Special, and the 63rd Parachute; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know if the VRS at that time had a similar arrangement, some kind of military department for contract soldiers to register?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with how they operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was there any prospect of being contracted to the Uzice MUP if one registered at the military department in Bajina Basta? Was the military department in Bajina Basta purely for the military, with different arrangements for registering with the MUP?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anyone registered with the military department in Bajina Basta was included in the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what the arrangements were, or if there were arrangements, for contract soldiers or contract personnel to register with the Uzice MUP at the time we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to deal with the special brigades and their involvement in the Skelani municipality. Now, first of all, according to Prosecution witnesses in this case --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's, Your Honour, JF-030 and JF-033.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- there were two principal occasions when the special brigades were engaged within the Skelani municipality. Firstly, in January of 1993; and in - secondly - March of 1993. I want to try to find out what you know about, first of all, the January 1993 involvement. You follow me?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In January 1993, the special forces crossed over into Bosnia, as they had been provoked by an attack on Skelani --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me pause you there first. I want to ask you some specific questions about that. The -- if I could just have a moment. The Oric indictment alleged that Muslim armed units had engaged in various military operations in eastern Bosnia between May of 1992 and February 1993, and that's when, according to the indictment, these various villages we spoke about yesterday had been plundered and when thousands of Serb individuals fled of area. Was it -- is it within your knowledge that that's -- let me rephrase that. Is that essentially your understanding, that Oric was operating between May of 1992 and February of 1993 in the villages along the Drina?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how should I put it? As regards the territory deeper inside Bosnia, I know there was war there. As for 1993, by that time, the conflict had reached the borders with the Republic of Serbia. So it is correct, what you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you, first of all, about the 72nd Special Brigade and what you know about its involvement in January 1993. Did you know, or do you know, that they received their training in Serbia and were trained by officers of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: A witness, JF-033 --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honours, page 25919.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- stated that -- and he was a member of that brigade - stated that they were trained along with the police from Knin in January of 1993 in Pancevo. Are you able to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: He --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I am approximately at page close to 20.000, so your reference to 25919 is -- comes a bit as a surprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'll make myself clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me just break that down a little bit. Did -- that Prosecution witness said that the police from Knin were being trained in Pancevo. Did you ever hear that the police from Knin in January 1993 were being trained by the VJ, or the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. The same witness then goes on to describe how on the 10th of January, 1993, as a member of the 72nd Brigade he attended a briefing in Kremna.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The same transcript, Your Honours, at 25923 and 25924.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And at that briefing in Kremna, General Mrksic, Commander Stupar, and General Ojdanic were there, and Mrksic briefed them that they were being sent to Bosnia. And I quote: "That they, the Bosnian Muslims, had taken the town of Skelani and that Serbia was in further danger and that's why they had to go there." Did you hear about this hearing from Mrksic setting out clearly to the brigade what the objective of the mission was?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You are familiar, though, with the objective, that objective being to liberate Skelani with the primary objective to prevent danger to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me try to shortcut things. Are you familiar, then, with the 72nd Special Brigade and the 73rd Parachute Brigade thereafter, in January 1993, attacking Skelani, the village, and other villages around the Skelani municipality?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The witness that I'm referring to, JF-033 --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Same transcript, Your Honours, page 25929.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- described how Skelani village and subsequently other villages were surrounded by the special brigades, and thereafter the combat operations began. Are you familiar with that, the tactic of encircling the villages, driving the combats -- combatants out of the houses, and thereafter engaging in combat? Are you familiar with that tactic used?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar of that tactic become used.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask you about this, then, instead. JF-033 also said that in relation to those people they found within the villages, "most of them were armed, some may have worn uniforms, others not, but if they were armed, they were no longer civilians."

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honours, page 25930.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Are you able to confirm that most of the combatant -- most of the men they found within those villages were armed?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can say that there was a lot of fighting, and they came across people who had weapons, and they engaged them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Are you able to comment on whether there were any women or children present in those villages at that time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know -- well, when Naser Oric launched a surprise attack, there were women and children there, because the villages were full. When our forces launched our counteroffensive operation, I had no information to the extent that there were women and children in those villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you hear about some of the sites that the special brigade saw when they went into the villages occupied by Oric's men? What I mean is that Oric had, I suggest, launched surprise attacks on those villages, massacred civilians, and left some of their corpses around the villages as a warning sign. Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During a briefing at the watch-tower, the commander explained the situation in the field to us. He told us that our forces came across many dead civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that it would not be logical for Oric, given what had happened previously, for him to have allowed women and children to remain in the villages when he was expecting a return attack? Would that be logical?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right, it would not have been logical for them to remain in the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: JF-033 claimed that a man called Lieutenant Zombi - his real name, I think, was Lieutenant Zoletic - had, during this attack, killed children. He was the only person who killed children.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Page 25930, Your Honours, of the same transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you hear about him? Is there any truth in that from what your -- from what you know?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear of that name or of anything like that happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: JF-033 also --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honours, page 26054.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- stated that he did not see anyone from the Serbian DB involved in those operations. Is that something that you can agree with, from your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, I want to move on to the second attack which, according to a witness in this trial, took place in March of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's JF-030, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, at the time of this -- these operations, March of 1993, where were you at this point? What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March of 1993, I think I was still a contract soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And your day-to-day? I'm trying to understand who you might have been in contact with and what you might have heard about these operations in March of 1993.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our area, there was no fighting or war-time operations. There was nothing of particular interest that was reported to the watch-tower as happening in the border area with Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Were you receiving information about the activities of the Uzice Corps, including these special brigades?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. We were not informed about that because it probably did not occur in our border belt area. So I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But let's see what you do or don't know. JF-030 --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is P2091, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- describes an attack, an unsuccessful attack initially, on a place called Miholjevine, M-i-h-o-l-j-e-v-i-n-e, on the 9th of March -- I beg your pardon, on the morning of the 10th of March, 1993. Did you hear about that unsuccessful attack by the 68th Guard Brigade, the 72nd Special Brigade, and the 63rd Parachute Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let me not waste time, then, and just ask you some more general questions to see if you know anything or heard anything about this. JF-030 --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Same exhibit, Your Honours, paragraph 52.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- states: "During these operations, to retake the municipalities, we did not fight against non-combatants. We neutralized the targets, including destroying the houses from where we received resistance. I know many houses were used by the enemy and there were civilians in those houses, but we did not kill directly any unarmed civilian during the fight." Are you in a position to be able to confirm what this witness said, that these operations in March of 1993 were aimed at military personnel?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose, since there was a war going on, military personnel was supposed to be neutralized, but I have no knowledge about this -- of this case, so I can't comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I would have expected you to announce that P2091 is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Oh, it's basically because I wasn't pulling it up I left that out, but yes, I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- let's be careful at least, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask you, then, about this, Mr. Plahuta. This same witness said that prisoners of war were taken and also civilians from villages were taken, and the prisoners of war went to Serbia, and the civilians either went to Bosnian army territory or to Serbia. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's, Your Honours, paragraph 52.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've heard nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, then: Are you able to confirm that the overall offensive operation was co-ordinated by Mrksic and Stupar with also some input by Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honours, page 57 -- paragraph 57.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the territory of Bosnia, that was probably the case, as these are the individuals who, on the whole, exercised command there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This same witness, at paragraph 58, says: "During our operation in eastern Bosnia, we were regularly supplied by ammunition, stores, and equipment from VJ. It was the Uzice Corps who provided this logistics support." Are you able to confirm that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's nothing I could say about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. This same witness, at paragraph 48, suggests that the Serbian PJM and Bozovic, leading a group called the Red Berets, was supposed to take part in these operations from Bajina Basta by providing mortar support. Did you hear about that intention?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The witness, though, then goes on to say, at transcript page 10739 to 10742, that he did not see and wasn't sure whether that, in fact, had taken place. Do you know if Bozovic or the Serbian PJM had anything to do with these March 1993 operations?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they had nothing to do with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: How do you say that with such certainty?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it's the special police unit from Serbia, I know that they didn't cross over into the territory of Bosnia, so ... I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But if Bozovic was working for the Republika Srpska MUP -- let me put that differently. What was the -- do you know what the role of the Republika Srpska MUP was in these operations within Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the situation was with regard to the Republika Srpska MUP. I don't know what they did over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. So your assumption about Bozovic is based on an assumption that none of the police units from Serbia was involved in the operations within Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Republic of Serbia MUP did not enter the territory of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And I'm going to press you a bit. I don't disagree with you, but I want to understand precisely how you know that and why you seem to be so certain about that.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, while I was at the watch-tower, our sector extended as far as the bridge that links Bajina Basta and Skelani. And at that location we co-operated with the police from the Republika Srpska MUP on the bridge. We would speak with them, we had contact, and at the watch-tower we were briefed and told that the MUP of the Republic of Serbia didn't cross over there, and this was confirmed at the border crossing by the policemen who worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I get the impression that this was a discussion -- let me put it differently. Why -- why was this a point of discussion? Was it -- would it have been something highly unusual if the Serbian police had crossed into Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, naturally, it would have been unusual. Of course, the Serbian police, if they had entered the territory of another state, well, that would have been unusual, because there was nothing for them to do there. So there was no need for them to cross over.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to come back to the Serbian police in a short while, but I just want to just finish with your knowledge of the special brigades and their involvement with the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If I can return, Your Honours, to P2091 under seal. This is JF-030 again.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This witness, Mr. Plahuta, testified that Mladic wanted to create a special VRS unit like the 72nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's paragraph 61, 62.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And to -- to summarise: Members of the 72nd Brigade were employed to train special -- a special unit of the VRS. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There's nothing I could say about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And at paragraph 68, the witness also testified that members of the VRS and MUP of the Republika Srpska were trained by the SAJ anti-terrorist unit in Batajnica? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Now I want to move on, then, to what you know about the -- or specific parts of your knowledge about the Serbian MUP involvement in Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have, please, on the screen P599. I think it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now just take a moment or two to read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You've read that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Were you aware of this order and this arrangement between the VJ and the Ministry of Interior of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of this. This was before I became a professional soldier, and I wasn't familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When you became a professional soldier and were working along the border, were you aware of Serbian MUP involvement along the border, first of all, trying to prevent paramilitary units entering Serbia? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was at the watch-tower, before the army started providing security for the border with Bosnia, the MUP, in fact, used to do that, so I know that they tried to crack down on crime, on trafficking over the border, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The order, at page 1 of the English and B/C/S, talks of the MUP of Serbia creating operations staff to take all necessary measures to prevent the activity of individuals, groups, and other paramilitary formations. Were you aware of these operations staffs being in place by the time you became a professional soldier?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that a MUP staff was established in the MUP building in Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And what did the MUP staff consist of, from what you could see? How many persons involved in this staff?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the MUP started using premises on the -- in the surroundings. Certain garages, for example. There were quite a few people. I don't know the exact number, but far more than before.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And from what you understood of that MUP staff, was it aiming at securing the border and restraining the activities of paramilitary groups in the border within Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm hesitating, Your Honour, because I'm -- can I just take instructions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm correct that Obrad Stevanovic was the commander of that MUP staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: He was interviewed by the Prosecution and stated - this is uploaded at 1D05492 - and stated the following. Page 5. "We engage police forces on the line of Prelovo, Dobrun, Strpci, Uvac, Ustibar, Sastavci, Strmac, and Kukorveci." Are you able to confirm that, indeed, the MUP staff did engage these police forces along this line to protect the border within Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they did do that, because Uvac, it's a little further south from where we were, but I think the MUP protected the border there. I don't think the army had a sufficient number of men. And the MUP covered part of the border there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you see that, or did you hear it? I want to understand how you know this.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there, but that's what they said at our watch-tower. Because in Bajina Basta there was still a competition for professional soldiers, as not a sufficient number of men had registered for that competition.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So it was your understanding that the Serbian police were engaged, effectively, because the army could not obtain sufficient men to protect the border?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic also says in that interview that this sort of engagement lasted up to the end of 1995 and beginning of 1996. Do you know if that's correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And Stevanovic, at page 2 of this interview -- at page 1. Let me just go back to page 1. That the Bajina Basta staff was formed on the 18th of January, 1993. I quote: "That's only two days after the event took place," that he previously described, "when ten persons were killed, 80 wounded, and more than 1500 people fled from Skelani to Serbia." Does that sound about right to you?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The staff was formed after the attack on Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And that, according to Stevanovic, was what gave rise to a training camp being formed on Tara for the training of the police with the assignments, and I quote, "that took place, if, in cases, for the case if the armed conflict would be spread from Bosnia to Serbia and which would allow the police to prepare to carry out such duties or activities in these -- in such circumstances."

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And then Stevanovic goes on to say: "Since bearing" --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honours, page 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: "Since bearing the fact that I was Chief of Staff of the staff in Bajina Basta, I informed the head of the sector of this problem and that was Mr. Stojicic. And he informed me that he would talk to the authorised civil and military authorised bodies in the RS in order to make an agreement along with the authorities in the RS crossing the border." And then he says that the Stojicic he's referring to is Radovan Stojicic. Can you confirm that this is the way it happened from what you understood: Stevanovic contacted Stojicic, Stojicic made the arrangements for the MUP staff and training camp on Tara. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Stojicic authorised the establishment of that training centre. And, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And then Stevanovic - and then we can finish with this - is asked, page 2: "Yeah, okay. Stojicic at that time was your direct superior as head of RJB." Stevanovic says: "Yes. The minister then decided -- the then-minister decided that Stojsic be my superior officer. I think the minister was Sokolovic." Was that your understanding of Sokolovic's role in all of this?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't know exactly whether it was Sokolovic, but perhaps it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... okay. Fair enough. I won't push you on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I just take instructions, and I think I'm nearly finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jordash. Is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine the witness, Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, you'll now be cross-examined by Ms. Harbour. Ms. Harbour is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, yesterday you testified that you trained at Mount Tara and then at Lipovica with a group of five people and these included yourself and also someone you called Sale. What were the names of the other three people?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Boris Plahuta, my brother, was there. There was someone called Slavisa. And the fourth man, I can't remember his name. He didn't spend much time training. And Sale was the fifth one. He gave us this training.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I'd like to talk to you now about your interactions with and knowledge of Mr. Franko Simatovic. You testified yesterday that you saw Mr. Simatovic for the first time in Bajina Basta in March 1993 on the terrace of the Drina hotel. And you said that your colleague at the watch-tower told you that this was "Franko Simatovic, an operations officer in the State Security Service, and he had said that he come there in order to set up electronic surveillance system." Was set up an electronic surveillance system a publicly known activity?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not. It was not a publicly known fact. But the army, or, we, at the watch-tower, did not have such a system in place at the time, and the soldiers were discussing the situation and goings-on and there were five or six of us there on that occasion having a drink, and one of my colleagues told me that about him. I don't know how he knew him, since I did not, and I can't tell you any more -- anything more than that. That's what I remember he told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Do you remember viewing a photo yesterday of Mr. Simatovic and a woman, which is now admitted as Exhibit D862?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If you'd like us to call up the photo, we can. I don't know if it's necessary. I would just like to know if you recognise the woman in the photo.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't recognise her. No, I don't know her.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: You've told us that the second time you saw Mr. Simatovic was in Petrova Gora in 1995. When precisely was this, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically on what date I saw him, but I think it may have been late May or around that time. I can't recall the date. In late May, in any case.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Stanisic in Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: When you saw Mr. Simatovic in Petrova Gora, you testified that he told you that he was an operative who was sent to unify the work of people working at the communications systems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think my learned friend misquoted. I cleared it up in the transcript who it was who said that. I would kindly ask my learned friend to check the answer first and then quote correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Karapandza told you that Mr. Simatovic was sent to unify the work of people working at the communications systems. These communications systems needed to be unified because people from different units under the Pauk Command were using them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had to unify their work because there were people rotating, as they couldn't be in the field all the time. That was probably the reason why.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Was that the only time you -- oh, excuse me. Did you speak with Mr. Simatovic at Petrova Gora?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not. Perhaps we exchanged a few words as I was filling up his tank, and we introduced ourselves, but that was the extent of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: After you left Petrova Gora in July 1995, you didn't see Mr. Simatovic again until you were in Pajzos, and in Pajzos you had no contact with each other; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: After you left Pajzos in December 1995, when was the next time you saw Mr. Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1996, during the ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Which ceremony are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the other unit was established, the unit we discussed. Shortly after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This was not the same ceremony you testified about yesterday where you met Vasilije Mijovic for the first time; right?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Vasilije Mijovic there for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Just for clarification: I believe yesterday we were discussing that ceremony as being in 1997. Was that actually in 1996?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The ceremony took place in 1997. What I meant to say in my answer is that I saw him when the unit was formed, and then shortly afterwards.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The answer is unclear.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: The interpreters did not -- were not able to fully understand your answer. When you say that you "saw him when the unit was formed, and then shortly there [sic] afterwards," did you mean to say that you saw Mr. Simatovic when the unit was formed in 1996?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see him in 1996. I saw him in 1997 at the ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: That's clear. Thank you. And you did not see him again until today?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't comment on that because I have not been given permission by my state to discuss it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question simply was whether you had seen Mr. Simatovic since 1997. Now, what is there in this question -- and we could move into private session if you would wish to do that. What is there in that question that would be outside the scope of what your -- have been given permission to, apart from whether that is binding upon this Court. Would you prefer to move in private session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, but I'd rather not make a mistake and that it be misunderstood later on. I saw him in 1998 when my brother was buried. That was the following time I saw him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May we take a break, Your Honour, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take a break. And we resume at a quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could I ask that we move briefly into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, how did your brother Boris die?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was killed in 1998 in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Under whose command was he at that time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The then-Commander Legija, or Milorad Ulemek.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could I ask that we move back into open session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We return into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I'd now like to focus on your time in the Uzice Corps of the VJ in 1992 and 1993. You've told us that you were transferred to the Perucac watch-tower, and you've told us that your job was to protect the state border, and your duties included patrolling along the border by the Drina river. By "patrolling," do you mean that you walked or drove along the riverbank.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We walked along the border.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Aside from patrols, you were also a sniper during this time; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did have a sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: What were your targets as a sniper based in the Perucac watch-tower?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have targets. It was standard procedure to have a sharpshooter in any patrol accompanied by another two members. It was a regular activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: What was it used it for? The sniper shooter.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, to defend the border in case of immediate danger either to us or the country.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: What MUP of Serbia units were involved in border control?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the police station in Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: You said earlier that at your watch-tower the soldiers and officers had to be kept up to speed regarding the activities of forces and of police. In order for you to carry out your border control tasks, you were no doubt fully familiar with the activities and responsibilities of all of the units along the border area where you were stationed; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's how it ought to have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This was for the entire time that you were in the Uzice Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour, the last -- the previous answer, "Yes. That's how it ought to have been," leaves some doubt as to how it really was. Could you please clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, when I asked if you were fully familiar with the activities and responsibilities of all of the units along the border area where you were stationed, you said: "That's how it ought to have been." Can you clarify. Is that how it was? Or were their exceptions?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were informed about police patrols. They did it in vehicles. They would provide some control or check-points of theirs to us. They informed us of whether they would stop at a certain location or not, from where they had a good vantage point between the two republics. This was in order to avoid friendly fire from us lest we encountered each other, especially at night. As regards the territory in our watch-tower area, we were informed of the police forces moving about. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: What border crossings would you have been informed about?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the bridge at Skelani, from that border crossing, up to the lake at Perucac.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If you know, how many border crossings were there -- how many places were there to cross the border between the bridge at Skelani and the lake at Perucac?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two places where one could cross by boat, although, at that time, they were not allowed to move from one side to the other. Only those two places had boat connections, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And how many places were there to cross by land? or over a bridge?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could cross a bridge at Skelani and across the dam of the hydroelectric plant at Perucac.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: You must have received regular information about any issues or problems with border control at the border -- these border crossings in addition to the Perucac dam and the Skelani bridge crossing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand the question fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If there were any problems encountered at any of the border crossings in your sector, were you informed about them?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think we would be informed all the time. Perhaps on occasion. Because it was the police who was in charge of border crossings, first and foremost.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: You've told us that -- about certain elements of the Uzice Corps Special Forces that crossed over the territory of Skelani after the attack by the ABiH forces in January 1993. Can you just confirm that you never crossed over that border in the operations following that attack?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: You've testified that police forces did not cross over, and at transcript page 19313, you said you were: "... in contact all the time with the police so I know -- I'm a hundred per cent sure that what I'm saying is true." Today you've reiterated this a few times. Just so we are completely clear on your evidence: You've said that you're a hundred per cent sure that Serbian MUP forces did not cross over into Skelani in January 1993. Are you also a hundred per cent sure that there were no Serbian MUP units already in Skelani?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no Serbian MUP forces there. When we came across police patrols before the attack, it's just that there were fewer of them at the time, but, still, we met, we always discussed what was going on on it's other side of the Drina, and they never mentioned that they crossed over. They would usually that they didn't know what was going on, since it was out of their jurisdiction. They had nothing to do with the other republic. I never heard any of their members mentioning any Serbian MUP forces crossing the border.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Are you also 100 per cent sure that no Serbian MUP units participated in the operations in eastern Bosnia while you were stationed on the border?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Such forces did not take part ever. The officers at the watch-tower never mentioned any MUP forces crossing the border, and I have never heard any policemen whom we met on patrols say that any MUP forces crossed over into the other republic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: During the combat operations, people were wounded. Wounded combatants were brought over the border from Bosnia into Serbia for treatment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: They were treated in the hospital in Bajina Basta?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's where they were treated.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: During your direct examination, you were asked about a number of Drina Corps and Uzice Corps documents related to operations in late January 1993. Is it correct that the Drina Corps and the Uzice Corps were both part of OG Drina?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly, but it is possible that they were together because Drina is the name of the river there. So perhaps the name they were given was based on the name of the river. But I'm not quite sure whether the same designation was used for them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Some of the documents that were put to you during your direct examination actually state that OG Drina included the Drina Corps and the Uzice Corps. You didn't know anything about this at the time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that they went by the same name, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I don't mean to confuse you. Just from your last answer, I'm concerned that I may have. So just to clarify this point, not to belabour it: When I say "OG Drina," I refer to "Operation Group Drina." So I'm not saying that the Uzice Corps went by the same name as the Drina Corps. Was that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not quite clear about this question about the name and about Drina operations group. Perhaps you could be a little more precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour, perhaps -- Were you aware of a operational group in which both the Drina Corps and the Uzice Corps were participating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Dragoljub Ojdanic was the commander and Dusan Loncar was the Chief of Staff of the Uzice Corps during your time in the Uzice Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragoljub Ojdanic was the commander of the Uzice Corps, but I'm not sure who the staff commander was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: The Independent Skelani Brigade participated under the Drina Corps in the operations that you've testified about in early -- or in late January 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably correct, that they acted together. They probably co-ordinated their action, so one could probably say that it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Well, the Independent Skelani Brigade is a brigade within the Drina Corps. So my question is whether you know that this particular brigade participated in the co-ordinated actions of the Drina Corps and Uzice Corps in January 1993.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Skelani Brigade did participate in the combat in January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade also participated in these operations; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know whether it was the light infantry brigade or whether it had some other name, but I know that they participated on the other side. I know that the Army of Republika Srpska participated in those operations from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Today the Stanisic Defence has asked you a number of questions about the attacks by the forces under Naser Oric on the Skelani area, and I would like to explore some of the prior attacks that occurred before the ABiH's attacks in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Can we please have P385 on the monitors.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This is Operational Directive number 4 of the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska, dated 19 November 1992. And this is a directive by Lieutenant-General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could we please have the bottom of page five in the English version and the top of e-court page 11 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I apologise, this is difficult to read in the original version, but it says: "The Drina Corps: From its present positions, its main forces shall persistently defend Visegrad (the dam), Zvornik, and the corridor, while the rest of its forces in the wider Podrinje region shall exhaust the enemy, inflict the heaviest possible losses on him, and force him to leave the Birac, Zepa, and Gorazde areas together with the Muslim population." Based on your experience in the Uzice Corps while that corps was participating in operations in Bosnia with the Drina Corps, were you aware that one of the tasks given by Ratko Mladic in November of 1992 was to force the Muslim population to leave this portion of eastern Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this. Gorazde, Zepa, Visegrad, if I have understood you well, all these towns were outside our area of activity, so I don't really know what they did up there. That's about 50 or 60 kilometres away from our sector, so I wasn't aware of anything of this nature. I know nothing about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could we please have Exhibit P392 on the monitors. And I'm interested in page 3 in the English and the B/C/S versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: While we're waiting for this to come up, Mr. Plahuta, I would just tell you that what we are about to look at is an excerpt from a notebook kept by Ratko Mladic, and you viewed a different excerpt of this notebook yesterday. And the particular entry that we'll be looking at is from Sunday, the 28th of February, 1993. The location is Tara. And the caption of the entry is: "Plan of action in Operation Udar." You are familiar with Operation Udar, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not. I'm not familiar with Operation Udar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: All right. Let's look further down in the entry where Mladic lists those that are present. He lists Panic, himself, Ojdanic, Loncar, Tkac, Frenki, and two men from the MUP. Do you know that Zivota Panic was the chief of the Main Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia at that time?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Panic was the chief of the Main Staff, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And you knew that Ratko Mladic was the chief of the Main Staff of the VRS during this time; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: You've testified that you saw Mr. Simatovic for the first time in Bajina Basta in March 1993 where he was concerned about setting up an electronic surveillance system. Did you know that in late February 1993 he was involved with your superiors from the Uzice Corps and the VRS and VJ leadership in planning an operation?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Further down in the entry, the first two lines say: "The units are in certain sectors and garrisons. "In Osmace, Jadar and Kragljivoda use PO and in Kragljivoda use napalm." You've testified that you were not familiar with Operation Udar; however, we see that Osmace is among the villages where the Uzice Corps was carrying out operations in January 1993, and, in fact, you marked this on a map and said that you were very familiar with the Uzice Corps's operations in this area. Did you know that fighting in Osmace continued after the Uzice Corps's January operations?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that because it was further away from the border areas so we didn't receive regular information about what was being done in the depth of the territory of the neighbouring state, neighbouring republic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: During your direct examination, when you marked on a map the positions and various villages where the Uzice Corps and the Drina Corps were engaged in operations, is it your testimony that you actually were not familiar with what went on during those operations?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I marked the territory, that was immediately after the attack on Skelani, when the Uzice Corps crossed over there with the special corps in order to liberate the territory. I can see that this is a later date. When that territory that I marked on the map was liberated, there were no longer any threats in that territory for the Republic of Serbia, so we didn't receive more detailed information in February on that date, let's say. We didn't receive more detailed information on action undertaken there and on who had remained active in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I take it your evidence was that by late February 1993 there were no threats to the Serb forces in that area?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our sector, there were no direct threats. There were indirect threats. There were always such threats. For example, if that part of eastern Bosnia remained in the hands of Naser Oric's forces, there was still an indirect threat to the town itself and to the territory of Serbia in general. But there wasn't a direct threat to the watch-tower, so we didn't receive any such detailed information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that there's something missing in the transcript, perhaps an important part of the answer, which is the part that concerns eastern Bosnia. In fact, the witness said something about the layout of the terrain, and that is not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we seek -- is that, Mr. Bakrac, page 33, lines 11 and 12? Is that where you think something is missing?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in fact, it's 12/13. Or, rather, 13 and 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... okay. Yes. Witness, there's a chance that part of your answer was lost in transcribing. I'll read to you what is now on the transcript, and please add anything you have said which is not in the transcript as I read it. The transcript reads: "For example, if that part of eastern Bosnia remained in the hands of Naser Oric's forces, there was still an indirect threat to the town itself and to the territory of Serbia in general." Up till here, anything missing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, and the interpreter apologises for omitting to mention it: The witness also mentioned the elevated nature of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that's apparently what you'd like to have added, Mr. Bakrac. Then he mentioned that in what context? because that's a bit unclear to me. About the territory? Or ... Being part of the threat due to the elevated terrain, is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I wanted to say. These forces in Osmace and Jadar, that terrain is evaluated, more evaluated than Bajina Basta, so it would be easier to fire on Bajina Basta from there than from some other position, or it would be easier to fire on the territory of Serbia in general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That being clarified, you may proceed, Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 6394 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This is a military document entitled: "Analysis of the Execution of Combat Operations in the Operation Encoded Udar." We've just discussed the planning, or part of the planning, of Operation Udar in the context of Mladic's notebook, and now we're turning to a document that addresses the conclusion of Operation Udar. Moving to page 2, we see a list of the forces engaged in Operation Udar. In the last group, under (a), from the corps, we see a list of forces for active-combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And the ones that I'm interested in are on the next page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: The Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade is listed, or the 1st Brlpbr, and the Skelani Independent Battalion is also listed. These are the two units that I asked you about previously which you testified also participated in the co-ordinated operations in January 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If we could have the bottom half of page 2 in the B/C/S version and the middle of page 3 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I'll read: "With Operation Udar, the liberation of the Serbian territories in the central Podrinje area was completed, while the enemy was squeezed into enclaves whose dimensions were determined with the engagement of UN forces (UNPROFOR)." Based on your previous testimony, Mr. Plahuta, this operation was not about liberating the eastern Bosnia region that had been the subject of the January 1993 operations because that had already been liberated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operation in January 1993 was conducted to liberate that part of eastern Bosnia and drive out Naser Oric's forces from that area. But I don't really understand your question; could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: You testified that the areas, particularly the area of Osmace which was evaluated, was no longer under a threat after January 1993, which is why you no longer had a need to receive information about operations in that area.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document as a Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, can I just have a moment or two to reflect on that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6394 will receive number P3118, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry could I just clarify: Is it the Prosecution's case - I just want to be clear on this - that Osmace was liberated in January 1993 and remained liberated through until past February/March of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Those questions were based upon the witness's answers, and we're seeking to know the extent of his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But I do think that if it's going to be put to the witness that Osmace was no longer a threat and at some point the Prosecution are going to rely upon that, to say, well, actually what WAS going on in Osmace in -- after January 1993 was forcible transfer, then we ought to know whether that's the Prosecution case or not. And I say that because of the evidence given by JF-030, which I assumed was consistent with the Prosecution case. And if I may refer Your Honours to P2091, under seal, and paragraph 54 through to 56, Your Honours will see why I might have come to the impression that the opposite was, in fact, the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution's case is that the goal of the operations conducted by the Uzice Corps in January 1993 and the goal of these operations, Operation Udar conducted in February 1993, was to drive the Muslim population out of eastern Bosnia, consistent with Ratko Mladic's order -- sorry, directive in November 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I, simply for the record, I note that this is, in our submission, a new case, because the case that they advanced up until this month was that which was consistent with the evidence of JF-030, or that's what we assumed. And JF-030 gave clear evidence in paragraph 54 that it was a combat operation to take Osmace, and, in fact, that combat operation had been directed at combatants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied against the admission into evidence. The Chamber relies on the -- of course, the main lines of the Prosecution's case, and not every word spoken by a witness which is sought is -- which is sought and admitted into evidence would not immediately change the Prosecution's case. Therefore, it's not a reason at this moment not to admit this document into evidence. Madam Registrar, was number already assigned to it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Number P3118 was assigned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then P3118 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, you -- I -- I explained to the Chamber and to the Defence what the Prosecution's case is. I'd like to put it directly to you to give you a chance to comment. Our case is that the goal of these operations conducted by the Uzice Corps in January 1993 and this further Operation Udar in February 1993 was to drive the Muslim population out of eastern Bosnia, consistent with General -- Lieutenant-General Mladic's November 1992 directive. And it is also our position that Mr. Simatovic's attendance at the meeting documented in Mladic's notebook shows that Mr. Simatovic participated in the planning of Operation Udar with knowledge of its purpose along with the highest level of VJ and VRS leadership. Are you able to comment on this?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said, the Uzice Corps crossed the Drina in order to fight, and not drive the Muslim population out. They wanted to drive Naser Oric's forces out of the area, as they presented an immediate danger to the Republic of Serbia. As for Operation Udar, I've already said that I cannot comment, since we were not informed of that -- about that operation. As regards the planning meeting attended by the military leadership and Franko Simatovic, it was beyond our level of knowledge. I wasn't informed at all with who planned the operation and how. We had no information to that effect. Simply put: We were simple border soldiers who were not informed about such things concerning the military leadership and the meeting described in Ratko Mladic's diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see that your microphone is on. I was wondering if there's -- no. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, you've testified at length about operations in the Skelani area that involved the VRS Drina Corps and also the Uzice Corps and, specifically, the 63rd Parachute Unit, the 72nd Special Brigade and the Guards Brigade, all of whom you testified wore red berets. And you've been very certain that there were no Serbian MUP units participating in these operations, and this is a point that I would like to explore with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 6491 on the screen. For the record, this was a document that was cited in the military expert report that the Simatovic Defence has withdrawn, and it's also on the Simatovic Defence bar table documents. And on the bar table documents it's listed as 65 ter 2D1607. We assigned a number 65 ter number simple so we could upload the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This is a report of the Skelani Independent Battalion, dated 25 February 1993, and it was sent to the Drina Corps Command and signed by Major Ilic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could we please turn to page 2 in the English and in the B/C/S. And we're concerned with item 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Under item 3, training and education, let's look at the last bullet point, which reads: "Regarding the training of recruits, somewhat more was accomplished in this area. A unit of the MUP of Serbia - the Red Berets - was stationed in Skelani as nearly all of the recruits received training in that centre for a period between one to three months." You did not know about this, did you, Mr. Plahuta?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. This is the first time I hear about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could we look now at the section entitled "Mobile Readiness" which is on page 4 in the English and on page 6 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: The last two sentences of this section -- are we -- sorry. There we go. The last two sentences of this section read as follows: "Between 27 January 1993 and 25 February 1993, about 500 ... conscripts were rounded up. As a result, the battalion now numbers around 800 soldiers, including two volunteer units (Radicals 60 and Red Berets 80 soldiers) under the command of the battalion." A Red Berets unit of the MUP of Serbia participated with the Skelani Independent Battalion in operations in January 1993; is that correct, Mr. Plahuta?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. As far as I can read what is in the document, I am not aware of it. I don't know about the Radicals or the Red Berets and whether they were in the Skelani Battalion. I know the Skelani Battalion existed, but I don't know what kind of structure they had within their establishment formation. Therefore, there's nothing I can say in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would now like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6491 will receive Exhibit P3119, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could I please have Exhibit P399 on the monitors.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, the document that I will be showing you is another document from the Skelani Independent Battalion to the Drina Corps Command. This one's dated several months later. And the date is 15 May 1993. The title of the document is: "Report on the Establishment of the Units for Special Purposes (Red Berets) of the MUP of Serb in Skelani." In the third paragraph, this report discusses the involvement of soldiers from the Red Berets camp in Jezero and Skelani, including three who were killed. Then they went on to Tara for further training. The documents that you were shown by Mr. Bakrac detail the Uzice Corps participation in operations in Jezero, and you marked this on a map to show us the line where the Uzice Corps and the Drina Corps linked up. Do you maintain that you did not know about the Red Berets participating in the operations in Jezero?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said already, I didn't know what the composition of the Skelani Corps was. Therefore, I can't comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: At the bottom of page 1 in the English and the middle of the page in B/C/S, it states: "The unit was under the command of Bozovic." You were asked today whether you knew if Bozovic or the Serbian PJM had anything to do with operations in March 1993, and you replied: "No, they had nothing to do with that." And then you were asked: "How do you say that with such certainty." To which you relied: "Well, if it's the special police unit from Serbia, I know that they didn't cross over into the territory of Bosnia ... I know that." And this is at temporary page -- transcript page 12 from today. Was it your assumption, or do you have knowledge, that Bozovic was affiliated with the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I don't know. I can't comment. I was only discussing the MUP of Serbia. I know they did not cross over, from my discussions with other policemen. I don't know about Bozovic. I'm not familiar with him, and I do not necessarily link him with the MUP of Serbia. As far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: You're testifying today that you're not familiar with him; however, yesterday you testified at length about his command over a tactical group in Pauk. And then when you reviewed certain JATD payments, you testified with no uncertainty that he was not a member of the JATD. It is the --

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not a JATD member. When I met him, he commanded the TG3 in Velika Kladusa. I know they were subordinated to the Pauk Command. As far as I know, they belonged to that tactical group. I believe it was the Army of Republika Srpska. As far as I know. I didn't spend much time there with them in order to know anything more than that, but I do know they were not part of the JATD. I mean, Bozovic personally was not in the JATD.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: It is the Prosecution case that, as this document shows, Bozovic was the commander of a Serbian DB special purpose unit in 1993 and he continued commanding Serbian DB units, including in Pauk, all the way through 1995. You've commented largely that you don't know about Bozovic's affiliations in 1993, but I wanted to put this case to you to see if you wanted to give any additional comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to object, but maybe I missed this in the document, but I don't think that the document says that Bozovic was a commander of a special -- DB special purpose unit at this time. It suggests that he was in some way connected to the Ministry of Interior of Serbia and his group was known as the Red Berets, which, I think, is somewhat different.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: The title of the document is "... Units for Special Purposes (Red Berets) of the MUP of Serbia ..." Is the issue with the fact that I said "DB" rather than "MUP"?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This having been clarified, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If we could now have the next -- oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. Plahuta, I wanted to give you a chance to comment on that. It is the Prosecution's case that Bozovic was a commander of a Serbian DB unit. This document says that he was a commander of a Serbian MUP unit. If you would like to make any comment?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't. I really don't know of him being such a commander. I know that he never appeared in the JATD unit. As of my arrival in the JATD onwards, I have no knowledge of him being a member.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Just a few more points that I'd like to look at in this document with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If we could have the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I'll continue reading: "In addition to apprehending persons who refuse to go to combat, they also control the bridge." And this is referring to this Red Berets unit under the command of Bozovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: You were guarding the border during this time, and you've testified about which VJ forces crossed the bridge between Bajina Basta and Skelani, and you've testified about which units were involved in control of the bridge. Isn't it true that a Red Berets unit had control of the bridge?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. On the Bosnian side, there was the Skelani battalion -- sorry, brigade. They guarded the border crossing on that side. I don't know which unit of theirs was in charge of that, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I'll continue reading in the document: "They took part in combat operations at Kragljivoda. Afterwards, they took part in the mopping up of the terrain around Radzenovice, when two soldiers from the unit, originally from Novi Sad, were killed." In the Mladic notebook entry that we looked at a few minutes ago, we saw a reference to Kragla Voda in the context of Operation Udar. And here we see a reference to this unit, this Red Berets unit, participating in combat at a place called Kragla Voda? I put it to you, Mr. Plahuta, that the truth is that Mr. Simatovic did not just participate in the planning of the counter-attack against Muslim forces but rather the unit that he and Bozovic commanded actually took part in that fighting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said already, in terms of Operation Udar, I can't offer a comment. We were not informed. And I don't know what the area was that was encompassed by the operation. As for Bozovic and Frenki, I really don't know. I never heard about that and was never told about that by anyone. It is my opinion that they did not take part. Perhaps someone would have told me something in the unit, some of the members, that they did take part. But as for the JATD, no one participated in the crossing over and attack on Naser Oric's forces, as far as I could learn in the unit. So I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't want to interrupt my learned friend. I simply wanted to mention to the Court that the English translation expands a bit the Serbian original. There is an abbreviation which is rather loosely translated in the English without a specific meaning being ascribed to the abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I take it that you question that, and that your comment whether it's loosely translated or not, that, first of all, we have to have the translation verified. That's the neutral way of introducing it. Now, I do not know what abbreviation you referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the last paragraph, beginning with: "They returned to the camp on the 14th of May." It is -- the abbreviation appears in that sentence. In the Serbian we only have the abbreviation; whereas in the English translation there is an expansion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look. Are you referring to the abbreviation "SBS" which appears in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Just immediately after, in the same line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then after the SBS, we get ... is that "MUP RS"? Yes, MUP RS --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... which --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We came across, as you know -- well, in this translation, this seems to be interpreted -- translated loosely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are seeking the assistance of the interpreters. We see "MUP RS," which is translated as "MUP of Serbia." MUP, Ministry of the Interior. Now, it is my experience that MUP RS could, depending on the context, could mean the MUP of the Republika Srpska. At the same time, RS also, sometimes, is used as an abbreviation for the Republic of Serbia. That is, Serbia. What I just said, have the interpreters any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We believe your reading of the abbreviations is correct, and the exact reference needs to be determined by the context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
