utterances.text: Thank you. That is now on the record, Mr. Bakrac. It is still to be considered, then, whether the context hints at the Republic of Serbia or the Republika Srpska, which is an entity in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I would note that in the B/C/S original in the heading of the document it says "MUP Srbije," if that assists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you are already hinting at the context. Mr. Bakrac, if there's any observation you'd like to make in terms of context, you have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, I could say something about the context now or later on during re-direct. As regards the key sentence, the context is completely different. There is a mention of the SBS command, which I believe stands for the Skelani Battalion, and it is stated that they could be commanded by the MUP RS. And that's what they were told as they were heading back to Skelani. From the text just preceding that area, we see that they arrived from another part of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Therefore, it remains an open question within the given context which MUP this actually is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the document before we take a break. The document is about a unit of the Republic of Serbia. Is that -- do you agree with that, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That's what's in the heading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the part we are reading from, that immediately preceding what happened the 14th of May, refers to the unit. Is that a unit in the context different from the unit in the title of this report, in your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. With your leave, I will discuss the details in re-direct, since -- well, I don't want to say anything in advance, but perhaps I could deal with it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah, but you issued -- you raised an issue of translation which you said was loose. We then established that it depends on the context what is the proper translation. So we're not talking about testimony anymore, but we're -- at this moment we are exploring the accuracy of the translation chosen here in the context, and I want to briefly explore that before you ask further questions about it. My question was: "The unit recently stayed in ..." that is still the same unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It seems be to the same unit. Yes, I'll stop here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, in the next paragraph there is an observation of what was said about the command over that unit. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, would it be logical in this context, where it is said that this unit, which we identified was a MUP of Serbia unit, would it be logical to interpret that they said that only the MUP of the Republika Srpska could be their commander? Would have any logic in this context, compared to that only the MUP of Serbia could be their commander? If we are talking about a unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. Because what we are doing -- you raised the matter yourself. What we are doing is looking at the context to find out what the appropriate interpretation is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, with all due respect, I beg to differ. For example, in the text -- please bear with me. The text above the sentence we are discussing. "All our attempts to return the soldiers of this unit to the Skelani Independent Battalion failed. The unit recently stayed in the dry border area around Visegrad," which is in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What does that change to the context I just analysed? That is, what is the logic about a MUP of Serbia unit stating that they only could be commanded by the MUP of Republika Srpska? Is that -- what's your logic in accepting that --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, and with all due respect, the entire text, in my view, points at the MUP of Republika Srpska, except for the heading, which mentions the MUP of Serbia. If we go through the whole document, in terms of military conscripts and everything else, it seems to me, in my modest opinion, that the context points at the other body. If we look at the heading, you seem to be correct. But if we exclude the title and look at the text alone, the context points at another direction. That is my modest opinion, Your Honour, and I can examine the detail -- the document in detail during my re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll re-read the document during the break. The translation was not loosely made, but you say is debatable. That is not exactly the same. We take a break and resume --

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Sorry, if I may. In the next section -- session I think that I will get to a portion where I ask the witness about parts of his personnel file. And in fairness to the witness, I thought that I should provided him with the file to review during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is no objection, please hand out or have a hard copy handed out to the witness. Could you please read that during the break, Mr. Plahuta, if that is possible, the document. If the usher would assist in giving it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do we have a translation of that, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] yes. Yes, it's in e-court. I can get the -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Oh, if it's there -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it the witness will read it in his own language. We'll take a break, and we resume at 20 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, while we are still on this document, I just have one last question for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If we could please turn to page 3 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This is a list of 52 persons from the Skelani municipality area in the Red Berets special-purposes unit. The date on the list is 9 April 1993. You grew up in the Bajina Basta area and you were stationed in this area for much of your career, leading up to, during, and following your stint in the Uzice Corps. I would like you to look over this entire list and let us know, first, if you recognise any of the names; and, second, if any of these people were members of the JATD, to your knowledge. So please take your time to read over the list, and let us know when you need to move to a different part of the page or to turn the page.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read through the page. It's fine. I've read through it all.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the names on this list?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the surnames. There a lot of surnames that come from our area, so to speak. But as for the first names, I think that it's only on the first page that I can recognise Maksimovic, Miroslav. If we're thinking of the same person. But I didn't recognise anyone else as being a member of the JATD, either on the basis of their surnames or of their first names.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that Maksimovic, Miroslav was a member of the JATD?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is the person in question, since a lot of individuals have the same first and last names, that I could recognise Miroslav Maksimovic. I could recognise that name, in fact. And to this day he is a member of the MUP. But I don't know if it's the same person. I don't know his father, whose name is Stevo. That's what it says. But Stevo isn't a name that you encounter frequently in our area. So I couldn't say that the person is the same person, but it's the same first and last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: The person by the name of Maksimovic, Miroslav that you know in the JATD, are you aware of whether he was in a Red Berets unit? During this time-period, I should clarify.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know whether he was a member at the time. I wasn't a member at the time. I didn't ask him about that. So I don't know what to say. I don't know if this is the individual concerned. It is the same first and last name as that of a member, but I can't say whether this is the person in question and whether this is the -- one of the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we provided notice in our filing of the 8th of May, 2012, that we would seek to tender a number of the personnel files of the individuals who are listed here as members of the Red Berets special-purpose units from Skelani municipality. I wanted to give the witness an opportunity to comment on any of the individuals that he was familiar with, and I'll leave the tendering of these documents for a rebuttal motion. Could we please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You wanted just the files to be tendered from the bar table?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, the question arises whether you -- from a procedural point of not -- or from a procedural point whether it would be, since the witness is here, something you would have to wait for the rebuttal stage. But I've no specific opinion about it, but apparently the Prosecution has decided to wait until that moment. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think in the interests of time, and also because the witness has not identified any that he recognised other than Miroslav Maksimovic, I think it would be more prudent to wait and just file it as a rebuttal motion. But, yes, to rebut this witness's and other Defence evidence led during the Defence case that there were no Serbian MUP units in Skelani. However if either the Chamber or the Defence wishes us to put these documents to this witness, we could do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think -- you are, I take, introducing that material as a challenge to the credibility or reliability of this witness, which is usually done when the witness is there. Now, I can imagine that you don't want to the put the whole of the personnel files of all these persons to this witness. But perhaps there are intermediary ways, like giving the names and say, Well, there's documentation about this, this, this, and this, do you still -- would that, in any way, change your testimony? which, of course, would the -- that's at least something one could consider, rather than to start discussing rebuttal evidence when there's not even further opportunity to ask the witness. And -- and it is directly cross-examining this witness on matters of credibility and reliability. So, therefore, I'm a bit surprised by the postponement of bringing this material, but I -- please consider it and think about it. And, Mr. Jordash, Mr. Bakrac, if the Prosecution would tender those personnel files in order to -- in order -- apparently on the basis of challenging credibility and reliability, would you consider that inappropriate or would you consider this -- from a procedural point. I'm not talking about content. Or would you consider it more appropriate to at least put to the witness any names of the persons of whom the Prosecution apparently intends in the future to -- to tender their personnel files? You may think about it as well. That's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, it's almost impossible to give a full or even an informed answer. Those files, I haven't -- we haven't got full translations of them. We don't know what it is the Prosecution say they show, what it is these men are alleged to have done, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Wouldn't it be a good idea, because otherwise we have a discussion very late on rebuttal, having no opportunity whatsoever that you would sit together, that the Prosecution explains what they would like to do at this moment apparently at the rebuttal stable and then to see whether it would not be from a point of view of procedural economy better to do it right away, and then to at least have an opportunity to ask the witness questions about it, and also to further examine the witness on matters you know the Prosecution wishes to tender in the future?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What I would say, aside from the issues that I've just highlighted, is that the first step would be for the Prosecution to indicate whether they say that the witness has knowledge of these people but is declining to provide that knowledge. The witness may not know, and the Prosecution may accept he doesn't know, but nonetheless, they want to -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... these files.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Refreshing the memory of a witness, of course, is not an uncommon thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But it wouldn't refresh the witness's mind if he -- if the Prosecution put the file to -- the witness has said, I don't recognise the name. Putting a file with the name and other details is -- is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you listened well to me, then I think I said that not perhaps by putting the file to the witness but to tell the witness, We have a file which states that the witness -- no, whatever. And you have to, of course, agree what that file suggests or states. And then to see whether the witness has any recollection on those specific persons. Could be. Could be not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, in a way, we're in a difficult position because, as Your Honours know, we object on first principles to the use of this additional evidence. So whether it's for credibility purposes or as fresh evidence for the truth of its contents, we would say the admission of this type of evidence at this stage is fundamentally prejudicial. Whether through the bar table, whether through rebuttal, or whether through cross-examination for credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I see that point. The matter for me is that a discussion which should be -- which we should have now or in two months from now. That's the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If the Prosecution say that this witness does know something about these people, then I think that they should put them to -- the files to the witness. We'll object as we always do, and the Prosecution can then use the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If allowed to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm kind of assuming on past practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But never anticipate on decisions not yet been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But for this discussion it might be important that you check whether there's a translation, that you check what claim the Prosecution makes in relation to that material, and to see whether that -- to see what the real points are, then, which remain in dispute. You have -- we're not sitting tomorrow, so there's some time, at least, to meet. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, you've given quite some testimony about border control and the units responsible for controlling the border in the section where you were stationed. And in particular, earlier today, at temporary transcript page 44 to 45, I asked you: "Isn't it true that a Red Berets units had control of the bridge." To which you responded: "I wouldn't know. On the Bosnian side, there was the Skelani Battalion -- sorry, brigade. They guarded the border crossing on that side. I don't know which units of theirs was in charge of that, though."

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Now, if I could please have 65 ter 6497 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This is a document from the Skelani Independent Battalion to the Drina Corps Command and the VRS Main Staff Command. The date on the front is a little hard to read, but we can see by the stamp on the second page that it was received on the 20th of June, 1993. And I'm interested in point number 6, which reads: "There have been no new attempts by Frenki's specials to move goods (tractors, technical appliances, weapons, and spare parts) across the bridge, but as a result, on explicit orders from the boss (Mr. Franko), the political and military leadership of Skelani municipality and the Skelani SB have been prohibited from entering the FRY (across the bridge)." Mr. Plahuta, wouldn't the control over who entered the FRY be in the hands of those who controlled the Serbian side of the border?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On our side, yes. The police from the Bajina Basta Police Station carried out controls. But on the Bosnian side, well, as to who they let through, we weren't responsible for that, and I couldn't tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Well, I put to, Mr. Plahuta, that, as this document states, Mr. Simatovic, Mr. Franko, and his specials were able to control and prohibit people from entering into Serbia, and, in fact, Mr. Simatovic was directly involved in the control of this bridge on both sides.

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what it says here, but I don't know anything about that. Can I see that the date is the 20th of June. At the time, I wasn't in the police force or in the military. That was in 1993. So the -- there's nothing I could say about that. But I know that on the Serbian side, well, every state controls enter into its territory. The MUP controls such entry. And on the other side you have the army or the police controlling entry. But I don't know what the situation is, or was, so I can't comment on what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't want to intervene until the witness had answered the question. But could my colleague please tell me where it says in the text that Frenki controlled crossings on both sides of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: The text says: "... on explicit orders from the boss (Mr. Franko), the political and military leadership of Skelani municipality and the Skelani SB have within prohibited from entering the FRY (across the bridge)."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So entering the SFRY over the bridge. I don't know how can you interpret that to mean from both sides of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, this is what apparently is prohibited, is movement in one direction at a certain point in time. Now, if you do not allow to cross a border, and this is, of course, to some extent a semantic discussion, then, of course, you stop at one side, you're not allowed to go to the other side, so linguistically ... but the example is clear that leaving the one territory in order to enter the other territory was prohibited in this instance. Mr. Bakrac, I think that whether that --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we have to ask the witness whether that changes in any way his answer. If Ms. Harbour would have just told you that Frenki controlled crossings, would your answer be -- have been any different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have said, the MUP of Serbia controlled entrance into Serbia. Whether anyone personally controlled things, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I think that if you want to further explore the matter, then you can do so in re-examination. Please proceed, Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could we now tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6497 will receive number P3120, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3120 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, you've given evidence of victims from the Serb forces who died during various operations in 1993 -- in various operations that we've been discussing, and I want to ask you about two of these victims in particular.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could I ask for 65 ter 6288.1 on the monitors. And, please, could we have the last page in both the B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This is a statement from the personnel file of Ljubomir Obradovic and it is on Serbian DB special-purpose unit letterhead. And in this one, unlike in Exhibit P399, it is clearly the Serbian DB under the Serbian MUP. And it's signed by unit commander Bozovic and deputy commander Zvezdan Jovanovic. Beginning at the top, this states: "On 9 April 1993, I was out in the Osmace area with an intervention group. At 1230 hours, I received information from Major Ilic, the commander of the Skelani TO, who commanded this line of defence, that the line had been broken through in the sector of Karacici and that his defenders had abandoned their positions." Osmace was one of the villages where the Uzice Corps was engaged in operations in 1993 and which you identified on a map, which is in evidence as Exhibit D862. I'll continue reading. "At 1245 hours, I set off with another ten men to mop up the terrain. In a co-ordinated action with the group which Bozovic brought, we managed to push the Muslims back from this sector. During the mop-up operation, we came across a Pinzgauer and, a hundred metres from it, the mutilated bodies of Zarko Teofanovic and Ljubomir Obradovic." And then it goes on to describe the circumstances which led to the death of these two individuals. And just to summarise: Teofanovic and Obradovic had gone to get food for their sector, then Major Ilic's men abandoned their front-line positions without telling anyone, and the Muslim forces ambushed Teofanovic and Obradovic as they were returning with food. Did you ever hear of this incident while the Uzice Corps was positioned in this area?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard about this incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, in our submission, this document indicates, first of all, that there was a Serbian DB unit in 1993; second, that Bozovic was commander of this unit; and third, that this unit was engaged in operations in eastern Bosnia in 1993. Do you have any comments on these points?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, I really am not aware of the fact that a unit from the RDB participated in action. I had information according to which the MUP didn't cross over and didn't take any action across the border, so I can't comment on this. I really know nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour, could I ask you one question. You explained to the witness what the Prosecution thought the document said. You said, "first ... there was a Serbian DB unit in 1993" in that area. Is that the unit described in the first sentences, "I was out in the Osmace area with an intervention group"? Is that the unit you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In our submission, this -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that's the unit. "Second, that Bozovic was commander of this unit," you said. When I read the document - and, again, the witness has said that he doesn't know anything about it - but in the fourth and fifth lines it is reads: "At 1245 hours I set off with another ten men to mop up the terrain. In a co-ordinated action with the group which Bozovic brought ..." Could you explain to me where the person who gives this statement says that he acted in co-ordination with a group Bozovic brought, whether still Bozovic is, in your position, the one who commanded the group of which the person who gave this statement was a member.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution's interpretation is that, as we can see from the letterhead, this pertains to a special-purpose unit, one special-purpose unit, of the MUP of Serbia DB, and this -- the commander of this special-purpose unit was Bozovic. The deputy commander was Zvezdan Jovanovic. And Zvezdan Jovanovic is the author of the report. He was out with a portion of the unit and met up with another portion of the unit that Bozovic brought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So when you answered my questions, you were not very accurate, because I asked you whether the intervention group was the unit. But what you actually say is that was a part of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That it was all -- both groups comprised one unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I better understand your position. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could we please have page 2 in the English version of this document, and page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This is a brief biography from the personnel file of Ljubomir Obradovic. It states in the second paragraph that on the 1st of December, 1991, he joined the TO of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem as a volunteer. And then on the 26th of December, 1991, he joined the special-purpose unit of the MUP RS as a reservist. And then it says that on the 9th of April, 1993, Ljubomir Obradovic and Zarko Teofanovic were killed in the Karacici sector, Osmace. And in the final paragraph, we see that: "His wife Tina Obradovic has been receiving his reservist's salary and a full daily allowance payment. The wife is the family contact person." And then it gives her address.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 6484, page 1. And once we 've viewed that document, then I will ask a question that pertains to both of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This is an excerpt of the personnel file of Teofanovic, Zarko. It states that: "He was a member of the reserve team of MUP Serbia special-purpose unit, that he was tortured and killed on 9 April 1993," again describing the same incident. And then in the last paragraph, it says: "Salary of the reserve team member, along with the full amount of combined daily expenses, is paid out to the spouse Teofanovic, Stojanka." Mr. Plahuta, did you ever hear of the Serbian DB paying the families of deceased members of special units?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard and I know that the MUP did pay some salary to the family members of the deceased, as is -- was the case with my brother. And it concerned members of the Serbian MUP. As for any members of the MUP in Bosnia, I really can't say anything in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could we now have -- turn back to 65 ter number 6288.1. And, on the first page, I do want to warn everyone in the courtroom that this is a photo of a dead body, and the reason I'm showing it is to see if the witness recognises the uniform. If we could just zoom in on the top photo in the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Do you recognise this uniform, Mr. Plahuta?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It resembles a military jacket. It may well be the M93 or M91 model. I think this is a military jacket.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Is this the same uniform that you wore as a member of the JATD?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a member of the JATD, I never had such a military windbreaker. Our pattern was different; more refined. I don't know what the exact name of the pattern was. In any case, it was a bit more elaborate and not as shiny as this one. I didn't have a jacket like this, although it was similar, to some degree, with a different pattern.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Your Honour, I'd like not to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I'd like now to tender this excerpt of the personnel file of Ljubomir Obradovic which is uploaded as 65 ter 6288.1, and I would note that an excerpt containing only the biography and the Serbian DB report signed by Bozovic is already in evidence as P3040, and the document uploaded as 65 ter 6288.1 adds this photo and also a hospital record indicating that this person was taken to the Bajina Basta hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We object. First of all, we submit that we ought to have had the disclosure of these names at the beginning of the case. In that way, we have been able to investigate who they were and what they are alleged to have done. Secondly, we ought to have had those names so that we understood what exactly is being said about the unit. On the face of the document 6288.1, there's a reference to at least two units. My learned friend has described the Prosecution case as being that they're one and the same units. One couldn't have told that from the document, but we now know that's the Prosecution case. We've had three years of a trial where we could have asked witnesses about these men and about this alleged unit. Secondly, we had no notice that the Prosecution was going to rely upon these documents today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Especially the last point, Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: These documents were in the list of documents that I noticed for use with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Apparently not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: That's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If that's the case, I will look into that. That was an oversight, and I apologise. Is -- is it perhaps noticed under P3040, which is already admitted, the excerpts of Ljubomir Obradovic's file.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, that is the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What does that mean? Of course, I do not know exactly this was part of it or whether it was in addition to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: The file that I'm seeking to tender includes two additional pages that are not in the admitted file of P3040. Those two pages are the photo and a hospital record showing that this victim was taken to the Bajina Basta hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's right. The new documents have not been noticed to us, basically. The hospital record, nor the photograph. While I'm on my feet, may I also inquire from the Prosecution - I think this is important for Your Honours' consideration - when these documents were obtained by the Prosecution and in which circumstances? When was the request made; and when were they received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have an answer to that, Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While the Prosecution is conferring, Mr. Jordash, your client left the courtroom. I take it that -- yes. May I take it that he waived, perhaps for a very short period of time, his right to be present? Otherwise we would have to stop at this very moment. Not knowing why exactly he left the courtroom, but if it would be just for a short sanitary stop. Would you agree that we'll continue for a couple of minutes and then see whether he returns?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, we can agree on that, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed. Ms. Harbour, any answer to the last question?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, that's something we'll have to look into further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that the two documents will be marked for identification. Madam Registrar, the numbers would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6288.1 will receive number P3121, Your Honours. And document 6484 will receive number P3122, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And are both marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 6492 on the screen. And I would note that this is a document from the military expert report that the Simatovic against has withdrawn, and it's also from their list of documents to tender from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: During your direct examination, Mr. Plahuta, Mr. Bakrac showed you a document that was from the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, which is now in evidence as D861. And at that time Mr. Bakrac informed the Chamber that it wanted to tender that document to show that "there were a number of Red Berets units, both in the Republika Srpska and Croatia, which had nothing to do whatsoever with the JATD of the Republic of Serbia." And I would like to explore that, which is why I'm showing you this order which is signed by Ratko Mladic as commander of the VRS on 13 May 1993, and it's sent to the Drina Corps Command and the Bratunac 1st Light Infantry Brigade. In the first paragraph, it reads: "In order to calm down the conflicts and incidents that happened between - illegible - unit of ... MUP of Serbia under the command of Vasilije Mijovic and Bratunac public security station and in order to stabilize the defence line and manning of 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, I order. "1, all military conscripts from Bratunac and Srebrenica area in the special units of Serbian MUP under the command of Vasilije Mijovic are to be put to the war-time assignment in the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade." My first question to you is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue. Looking at the original and being very alert on any reference to RS, I see what is here in English "unit of the RS MUP." Looks as if in the original it refers to the Republike Srbije, which I understand is the Republic of Serbia rather than the Republika Srpska. And in order to avoid whatever confusion, I'm wondering whether the parties would agree that RS MUP here must be understood to be the Republic of Serbia MUP. I saw Mr. Bakrac was already nodding "yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yes, Your Honour. I can confirm that in the original we can find the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you do not oppose that interpretation, then, Ms. Harbour. And Mr. Jordash, I think, would agree it as well. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fact, I have requested a correction of this translation, and we will upload that as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think everyone would agree that that would be the appropriate way of proceeding, but I wanted to clarify it already now. Please proceed. Because you were about to ask a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, did you know, as Mladic acknowledges here, that in the first half of 1993 Mijovic commanded special units of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If we go down to point 3, it states: "The entire unit commanded by Mijovic in the previous combat activities is to be subordinated to the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade and form the Sabotage Detachment of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade from its members, that should be used for the sabotage and intervention actions in the brigade AOR." Did you know that, as Mladic has stated, even prior to this order the Serbian MUP special units commanded by Mijovic had participated in combat activities?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: For your reference, and the reference of the Chamber and the Defence, an order signed by the commander of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, Colonel Vuksic, on the 15th of May, 1993, refers to and implements this order from Mladic. And that is in evidence as P1081.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6492 will receive number P3123 [Realtime transcript read in error "P3213], Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3213 [sic] is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could we please now have 65 ter 6493. And this is also from the Defence military expert report which has been withdrawn, and it's also on the list of documents that the Simatovic Defence seeks to tender from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, I would just like to correct. I see on the record that you said that 6492 is P213 [sic]. Actually, the number received is P3123.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then I -- in order to make no mistake, I read from the transcript. But apparently there's a -- perhaps a joint error, then. It's now corrected. And it is ... Could you please repeat it, Madam Registrar, because again it appears not fully on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I repeat. So number 6492 receives number P3123, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3123 is admitted into evidence. The other number is, therefore, to the extent it was already registered, is vacated. But this is the exhibit number for this document. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could I please have 65 ter 6493. And there it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Mr. Plahuta, the Simatovic Defence has suggested that Mijovic's unit in the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade has nothing to do with the Serbian MUP. This document from the Drina Corps Command is addressed personally to the president of the Bratunac Military Assembly and is dated on the 27th of November, 1993, which is six months after Mladic's order resubordinating Mijovic's unit to the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. I will read from the bottom of the first passage in English, which is towards the middle of the page in the B/C/S. "The appearance, as you say, of Major Vasilije Mijovic in the area of the Bratunac municipality, is not linked," and we move to the next page in English, "to any document or an oral order of this command, which automatically means that this command has never issued any order to the mentioned. "Vasilije Mijovic is not registered in the military records of the Bratunac Brigade, nor of this command, on any basis, which makes him a person who can either be a paramilitary or on the strength of the MUP or on a work obligation." And, finally, if we could look to the bottom of the page in English and move to the second paragraph of page 2 in the B/C/S, it states: "A clear conclusion can hereby be drawn: No Mijovic's unit can be made out of the available manpower of the brigade because the establishment of a light infantry brigade does not envisage any such formation." Now, in light of this document and the other documents I have shown to you today, I put to you that Serbian MUP units under Mijovic were involved in operations leading up to and following the attack in January 1993 by the ABiH forces and that Mijovic's unit remained ultimately under the command of the Serbian MUP, even while it was operationally resubordinated to the Bratunac Lpbr. Do you have anything to say about this?

utterances.speaker: DEJAN PLAHUTA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have a comment about this because I never heard about any of the things mentioned here, so I know nothing about it. I have no comment. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could I please tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6493 will receive number P3124, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you said P-- THE REGISTRAR. It's again --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. P3124 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Could we now have 65 ter 6494 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: During your direct examination, you commented on a 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade document from October 1994 which referred to the commander of the Red Berets platoon, Bosko Neskovic. Your conclusion was that Neskovic was never a member of the JATD unit of the Serbian MUP. There's evidence in this case that Bosko Neskovic actually commanded a Red Berets group that arrived in Bratunac in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And I'm referring to P2104, for the reference of the Chamber and the parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: The document that you see on the screen before you is from Bosko Neskovic's personnel file from the Serbian DB. As we can see, the date on the top of the file is 2 June 1992. And if we turn to the second page, you see that the file contains the same form that was found in the file of Branko Pavlovic, which is now in evidence as D864, which you said was not familiar to you. Having viewed this file of Bosko Neskovic, do you agree that you simply are not in a position to know whether Bosko Neskovic was in a Serbian MUP special-purposes unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the witness answers, I would kindly ask my learned friend to ask him -- or, rather, to tell us whether she has in mind the entire period from 1991 to 1995, or does she have a specific shorter period in mind, just so that the witness is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And could I add to that, just so that we're all clear, because I've got no idea from the notice we've been given, what the Prosecution's case is concerning when Neskovic was in a special DB unit and where and what alleged -- is alleged to have done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour, the questions about this person were put to the witness in a certain time-frame, context, which might not necessarily be the same as the document we saw before, and I have not been able to decipher this document yet. Would you please, when you put further questions to the witness in relation to these documents, keep that clearly in mind so that there's no confusion whatsoever. The previous document was, I think, about June 1992, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Is Your Honour referring to the first page of this file?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether it's the -- the -- the page we saw on our screen a minute ago with the very small table. Again, but perhaps I give you two some time to think about it. You're now aware of the problems the parties have expressed. It's a quarter to 2.00, so we have to finish for the day. Could you give us an indication on whether you're on track as far as time is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will check with the representative of the Registry to see how much time I have used. I do think I will use the full three hours originally anticipated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which, I would say, opens the possibility to perhaps even conclude the testimony of this witness in the next hearing day, which is on Thursday and not tomorrow. Let's try to see whether that can be achieved. And I'm of course also addressing the parties who will re-examine and perhaps further cross-examine the witness. Then, to the extent the transcript is not clear or to the extent I have not been very clear, P3124 was admitted into evidence. We said something about the number. Then, Mr. Plahuta, we'll not hear this case tomorrow. We will continue on Thursday, the 17th of May, at a quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon in this same courtroom, II. We'd like to see you back then. We'll see whether it's possible to conclude your examination on that day. And I really urged the parties, because if, just for 20 minutes, if the witness would have to wait for another couple of days, that's something we should try to do our utmost best to avoid. Mr. Plahuta, I give you the same instructions as I did the previous days, that is, that you should not speak or communicate in any way with anyone about your testimony. Then we adjourn, and resume on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just have two questions I would like to put to you. I have been given a personnel file to read. Can I take it away with me, or should I leave it here? And if the Prosecution or Defence have any questions about the personnel file, since it might be necessary to explain certain things, and given that there are places and individuals who have to be mentioned in relation to the personnel file, I believe that this should be done in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It depends on what it exactly is. We have certain -- certain rules for that. Would you like to receive the personnel file back until Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I think that that would be best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The appropriate way to -- the personnel file to be returned to Ms. Harbour at this moment. But then, well, you've read it. And I take it that the witness may consult it on Thursday, if any further questions are put to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then if you leave it on that desk, then it will be returned to Ms. Harbour. We stand adjourned. And we resume on the 17th of May, at 2.15 in the afternoon.
